summary: Chrono & Spatial is an interactive astronomical platform that transforms real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations into a dynamic view of the changing universe. Using NASA/IPAC IRSA and NASA JPL data, it aligns and compares multi-epoch observations to investigate moving asteroids, comets, variable stars, and transient astronomical events. With scientific difference maps, statistical change detection, orbital cross-matching, and collaborative citizen-science classification, the platform makes complex astronomical data more accessible and helps people investigate how the infrared universe changes over time.
details:
Overview

Chrono & Spatial is a scientific web platform developed for NASA's Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It addresses a fundamental problem in astronomical exploration: individual sky images show what the universe looks like at a particular moment, but comparing observations across different epochs can reveal how celestial objects change, move, appear, or disappear.

NASA Data Integration

The platform integrates genuine SPHEREx Level-2 calibrated spectral image products from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). It uses the Simple Image Access (SIA2) service to discover observations by celestial coordinates and the Image Bounded Extraction (IBE) service to retrieve FITS cutouts.

SPHEREx uses six detector arrays with Linear Variable Filters, covering approximately 0.75–5.0 micrometers through 102 effective spectral channels. Chrono & Spatial preserves detector, wavelength, observation-time, and celestial-coordinate metadata throughout its processing workflow.

For solar-system object investigation, the platform integrates NASA JPL's Small-Body Identification API, Horizons ephemerides, and Small-Body Database (SBDB). These services help identify known asteroids and comets, retrieve their predicted positions, and obtain orbital information. NASA's NeoWs API is also integrated for supplementary near-Earth-object information.

Scientific Processing

The Python science engine performs World Coordinate System (WCS) reprojection to align observations onto a common celestial grid. It checks wavelength and calibration compatibility, estimates and subtracts background variations, propagates detector variance, and generates calibrated flux-difference and statistical significance maps.

Potential changes are extracted using photutils DAOStarFinder, with detected pixel positions converted into J2000 celestial coordinates. The resulting candidates can be investigated against JPL orbital and ephemeris information. A detected candidate is treated as an investigation target, not automatically as a confirmed astronomical discovery.

Interactive Features

  • Interactive sky exploration with celestial coordinate navigation and observation metadata.
  • Detector-band selection and multi-epoch observation browsing.
  • Time-based exploration with timeline animation and crossfading.
  • Side-by-side, swipe, blink, and scientific difference-map comparison modes.
  • Moving-object identification and orbital information through NASA JPL.
  • Citizen-science candidate classification with community agreement tracking.
  • Operations dashboard for API health, database connectivity, processing jobs, worker activity, and storage.

Technology and Architecture

The project uses a decoupled three-tier architecture:

  • Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, and Zustand.
  • Backend: Node.js, Express, TypeScript, MySQL, mysql2, and Zod.
  • Scientific processing: Python, Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, photutils, Pillow, Requests, and PyMySQL.

The Express backend manages API requests, NASA integrations, database operations, and file delivery. A separate asynchronous Python worker handles FITS ingestion, scientific image processing, candidate extraction, and JPL cross-matching through a database-backed job queue.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Chrono & Spatial connects real NASA astronomical observations with scientific image analysis and accessible visual exploration. It helps students, astronomy enthusiasts, and citizen scientists investigate changes in the infrared sky without needing to manually process complex FITS files or independently operate multiple astronomical APIs.

Its key innovation is bringing multi-epoch infrared comparison, statistical change detection, solar-system object identification, and collaborative human review into one platform. The result is a more accessible and transparent approach to exploring a dynamic universe.
